description: AgriGuard is a hackathon prototype that tackles slow, opaque crop-insurance claims for wheat heat damage. It uses hourly FortyGuard temperature data and a fixed rule (34 °C or higher for 3+ hours) to automatically decide if a heat event occurred, then records the evidence and a simulated payout. The AI agent only explains the result and can't change it.

details:
The real-world challenge

  • Heat can ruin wheat fast. A few hours of extreme heat during flowering or grain filling can cause serious crop damage.
  • Traditional claims are slow. Parametric insurance (paying out when a measurable trigger is hit) can be faster, but only if everyone trusts the trigger.
  • Lack of transparency. Many systems just show a weather chart. They don’t show where the data came from, which rule applied, what event triggered, and why a result was recorded. Growers, insurers, and reviewers need that full decision path to trust the outcome.

The technical challenges it addresses

  • Keeping AI out of financial decisions. The policy result and payout are calculated by a deterministic TypeScript engine, not an LLM. The AI agent is only allowed to explain the evidence through a small set of server-controlled tools, so it can’t alter a payout.
  • Avoiding duplicate payouts. Repeated monitoring runs could create the same payout twice, so the system uses an idempotent payout key to record only one per qualifying event.
  • Handling bad or missing data. The temperature adapter is fail-closed: if data is missing, stale, or invalid, it returns “data unavailable” and creates no payout result.
  • Separating real from fake data. The interface clearly distinguishes verified FortyGuard data from the synthetic fallback.
  • Making it auditable. Observations, policy values, timing, heat score, result, and source are stored together in one persistent evidence record.
